sources.title: A novel rapamycin analog is highly selective for mTORC1 in vivo.
limits: Complex-selectivity and metabolic/immune endpoints; no reproductive protection established.
Testis is absent from the reported eleven-tissue panel.

sources.title: The rapamycin analog Everolimus reversibly impairs male germ cell differentiation and fertility in the mouse†.
limits: Official primary abstract only; fullTextXML returned HTTP 500.
Recovery varies by endpoint; mouse findings are not a healthy-human risk estimate.

sources.title: Rapamycin-mediated mTOR inhibition impairs silencing of sex chromosomes and the pachytene piRNA pathway in the mouse testis.
limits: Adult-mouse study with both complex responses; not a human analog safety result.

sources.title: mTORC1/rpS6 signaling complex modifies BTB transport function: an in vivo study using the adjudin model.
limits: Official primary abstract only; fullTextXML returned HTTP 500.
Main anatomical argument instead uses the successfully read Sertoli-study Figure 1.

sources.title: Brain-restricted mTOR inhibition with binary pharmacology.
limits: Brain-restricted mouse pharmacology; not systemic geroprotection or testicular protection.
Reviewed body contains no testis, testes, sperm or fertility term.

sources.title: Cholesterolated Rapamycin Prodrug Liposomes Induce Antigen-Specific Tolerance and Enable AAV Redosing.
limits: Official primary abstract only; no testicular free-drug or reproductive result supplied there.
IV liver-accumulating formulation is not oral systemic delivery.

sources.title: Mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) pathway in Sertoli cells regulates age-dependent changes in sperm DNA methylation.
limits: Cell-specific genetic knockout, not a rapalog treatment trial.
Testis weight and measured sperm endpoints diverge; sperm motility was not assessed.

sources.title: Topical rapamycin reduces markers of senescence and aging in human skin: an exploratory, prospective, randomized trial.
limits: High attrition and small analyzed subsets.
Blood non-detection at one sampled visit is not zero exposure or a complete PK profile.
No reproductive or systemic aging result established.

sources.title: Sirolimus may reduce fertility in male renal transplant recipients.
limits: Observational transplant population, not otherwise healthy users.
Recovery is not guaranteed by the six-person interruption subgroup.

prior_review_reference.context: Germ-cell mTORC1 requirement cited in the earlier oral-targeting feasibility review.
prior_review_reference.access_scope: Previously reviewed source, not a new full-text retrieval in this continuation.
